It is also possible that the meaning is: on that day it reports by reporting that your Lord inspired it with its news, since its reporting that your Lord inspired it is a reporting of its news, just as you say, "You advised me every advice, in that you advised me in religion." It is also possible that *bi-anna rabbaka* is a substitute for *akhbaraha* (its news), as if it were said: "On that day it will report its news, that your Lord inspired it," because you say, "I told him such-and-such" and "I told him of such-and-such."

*Awha laha* means *awha ilayha* (inspired to it), and it is a metaphor, like His saying ﴿that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾. The poet said:

*Awha lahā al-qarāra fa-staqarrat*
(The settling inspired it, so it settled.)

[Note: The explanation of this verse was given earlier, on page 75 of the third part; refer to it if you wish. Its corrector (muṣaḥḥih).]

Ibn Mas‘ud read *tunabbi'u akhbaraha*, and Sa‘id ibn Jubayr read *tunabbi'u* with the lightened form. ﴿People will come forth in scattered groups﴾ from their places of exit from the graves to the place of standing: some with bright faces, secure, and some with dark faces, terrified. Or they come forth from the place of standing in scattered groups, and the two paths of Paradise and Hell separate them, so that they may see the reward of their deeds. In the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ) it is *liyaraw* with a fatha. Ibn ‘Abbas and Zayd ibn ‘Ali read *yarahu* with a damma.

It is related that a Bedouin delayed *khayran yarahu* (good, he will see it), and someone said to him, "You have put first and last." He said:

*Khudhā baṭna Harshā aw qafāhā fa-innahu*
*kilā jānibay Harshā lahunna ṭarīq*

(Take the belly of Harsha or its back, for both sides of Harsha have paths for them.)

[Note: It was related that a Bedouin delayed the words of God, ﴿good, he will see it﴾, after what follows it, and it was said to him, "You have put first and last," so he struck that verse as an example. Harsha, with the vowel pattern of Sakra, is a mountain pass on the road to Mecca near al-Juhfa; that is, take the path of that pass or what lies behind it, for indeed the matter is that each of its two sides is a road for the camels you seek. The repetition of the word "Harsha" is to fix it in the listener's mind, lest he be inattentive to it, and the context was one of guidance, so repetition there was fitting.]

*Al-dharra* is the small ant. It is said that *al-dharr* is what is seen in the sunlight as dust. If you ask, "The good deeds of the disbeliever are nullified by disbelief, and the bad deeds of the believer are forgiven by avoiding the major sins; what is the meaning of being recompensed with the weight of an atom's worth of good and evil?" I answer: the meaning is: whoever does an atom's weight of good, from the group of the blessed, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil, from the group of the wretched, because it came after His saying ﴿people come forth in scattered groups﴾. [Note: Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask, 'the good deeds of the disbeliever are nullified by disbelief…' etc." Ahmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: The question is built on two premises. The first is that the good deeds of the disbeliever are nullified by disbelief, and this requires examination: the good deeds of the disbeliever are nullified in that he is not rewarded for them and is not granted bliss. As for lightening punishment because of them, that is not rejected, since sound hadiths report it. It is reported that Hatim is lightened for his generosity and kindness, and this is also reported concerning others, such as Abu Talib. So the good deeds of the disbeliever have some effect in lightening punishment, and the thing seen may be that effect, and God knows best. As for the second premise, that avoiding major sins necessitates the purification of minor sins and their expiation for the believer, this is rejected according to the People of the Sunna, for minor sins, in terms of expiation, have the same ruling as major sins: they are expiated only by one of two things, either sincere accepted repentance or God's will, and nothing else. Avoiding major sins does not, according to them, require the expiation of minor sins. So the question is void for the People of the Sunna, but al-Zamakhshari bound himself to answer it, so they hold him to his corrupt premise. God grants success.]

[Note: It is a hadith of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat *Idha Zulzilat* four times has recited the whole Qur'an." Recorded by al-Tha‘labi from a hadith of ‘Ali through the chain of the People of the House, but it is through the narration of Abu al-Qasim al-Ta'i, and it is void. Its witness is in Ibn Abi Shayba and al-Bazzar through the narration of Salama ibn Wardan from Anas, traced to the Prophet: "*Idha Zulzilat* equals a quarter of the Qur'an." It was also recorded by Ibn Mardawayh and al-Wahidi through their chains to Ubayy ibn Ka‘b, with the wording: "Whoever recites *Idha Zulzilat* is given the reward of one who recites the Qur'an."]

Medinan, though some say Meccan; it has 8 verses [revealed after Surat al-Nisa']. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) quaking﴾. Zilzalaha is read with a kasra and with a fatha on the zay. The kasra form is a verbal noun (maşdar), and the fatha form is a noun. In the morphological patterns, *fi‘lāl* with a fatha occurs only in doubled roots. If you ask, "What is the meaning of zilzaluha with the genitive (idafa)?" I answer: it means the quaking that its nature and God's will require, which is the most severe quaking after which there is none. A similar usage is your saying, "Honor the pious person with the honor he deserves, and humiliate the sinner with the humiliation he deserves," meaning: the honor and humiliation that they merit. Or it means its whole quaking and all of what is possible of it.

﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾. Al-athqal is the plural of *thaql*, which is *matā‘* (goods). Al-Sihah (the lexicon of al-Jawhari) says: "*Al-thaql* is the singular of *al-athqal*, like *himl* and *aḥmāl*. *Al-thaql*, with a vowel on the first letter, is the traveler's goods and household." [Note by the editor: (ʿ).] It refers to the goods of the house. ﴿And brings forth its burdens﴾ means that it makes what is in its belly of treasures into burdens for it.

﴿And man will say, "What is wrong with it?"﴾ It is shaken with this severe quaking and throws out what is in its belly. This occurs at the second blast, when it quakes and brings forth its dead alive. They will say this because of the terrible matter that overwhelms them, just as they say, "Who has raised us from our sleeping place?" It is said that this is the words of the disbeliever, since he did not believe in resurrection. As for the believer, he says, "This is what the Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke truly."

If you ask, "What is the meaning of the earth 'reporting' and of revelation to it?" I answer: it is a metaphor for God's causing in it states that take the place of reporting by speech, so that the one who says "What is wrong with it?" looks at those states and understands why it quaked and why it threw out the dead, and that this is what the prophets used to warn of and caution against.

It is also said: God makes it speak in reality, and it informs about what good and evil was done upon it. It has been narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that it will bear witness against every person about what they did upon its back. [Note: Recorded by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim, through the narration of Ibn Ayyub from Yahya from Abu Sulayman al-Minqari from Abu Hurayra. Sa‘id is trustworthy. Rushdin ibn Sa‘d, who is weak, contradicted him, saying: from Yahya ibn Abi Sulayman from Abu Hazim, through the two chains mentioned, from Anas ibn Malik. It was also recorded by Ibn Mardawayh.]

If you ask, "What governs *idha* and *yawma'idhin*?" I answer:

*Yawma'idhin* is a substitute (badal) for *idha*, and both are governed by *tuhaddithu* (it will report). It is permissible for *idha* to be governed by an implied verb and for *yawma'idhin* to be governed by *tuhaddithu*.

If you ask, "Where are the two objects of *tuhaddithu*?" I answer: the first has been omitted, and the second is its reports. The original would be: "it reports its reports to the creation," but the intended point is the mention of its reporting the news, not mention of the creation, in order to glorify the day.
